dedupe_keys.name: esa space environment report annual statistics on objects and debris in earth orbit

description: The Space Environment Report is published every year since 2017 by the Space Debris Office of the European Space Agency to give a transparent overview of global space activity and of how well debris mitigation measures are working. The 2025 edition, read on 2026-09-28 and based on data collected to the end of 2024, reports about 40,000 objects tracked by space surveillance networks, of which about 11,000 are active payloads, an estimated 1.2 million debris objects larger than 1 cm, and around 550 km altitude as many threatening debris objects as active satellites, based on ESA's MASTER model; it charts fragmentation events by cause, re-entries of intact objects more than three times a day and adherence to mitigation standards. Coverage is all of Earth orbit, in annual time series by orbit regime. Access is a free web overview with the full report as a PDF; ESA's general terms of use apply and no specific licence is named on the page. Caveats: the report aggregates catalogued objects and model estimates, and small debris counts are statistical estimates, not observations. It supports hazard exposure and resilience analysis of satellite communication, navigation and Earth observation services on which infrastructure depends. Related records: data-esa-discos is the object database behind it and model-master-space-debris-environment-model the debris model it uses.
